_README: Statement-wave assignments for v2 rows authored after X1 reconciliation. build_v2_manifest.py merges these rows into the manifest, assigns phase/repo/formal_name/source-verification metadata, and drives the statement=done overlay entries. Opt-in per-row hash pin (plan WP3): `source_hash` records the corpus statement text the second reader actually read, and `source_verified_by`/`source_verified_at` override the file/wave-level values for that row. build_v2_manifest.py exits with "source text changed since verification; re-verify" when the upstream text is later reworded, so a silent corpus edit can never leave a statement leg `done`.

axv_2307_15512_00.note: Erde-Kang-Lehner-Mohar-Schmid Conjecture 1.4: the cop number of a connected k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices is O(sqrt(n/k)). The cops-and-robbers game is defined locally in the new shared foundation hypergraph-theory/theories/foundations/hypergraph.v as a finite-horizon cop-win closure on positions: [hg_win E m C r] is a Boolean fixpoint on the number of remaining rounds (cops move first along [hg_move] = stay or step to a vertex of a common hyperedge, catching the robber the instant one lands on him; then the robber moves the same way), [hg_cop_win E c] existentially quantifies the placement and the horizon, and [hg_is_cop_number E c] says c cops win and no fewer do. Structurally the same shape as the graph game written concurrently in graph-theory-misc (no dependency between the packages). O(sqrt(n/k)) is a single absolute constant C quantified outermost, squared to clear the root: c^2 * k <= C^2 * n. Guards: 0 < k and k <= #|T| (the edgeless one-vertex hypergraph is vacuously k-uniform for every k and would refute the unguarded body; every hypergraph with a hyperedge satisfies k <= n, see grounding_X217.v).

X217:hypergraph-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. axv_2307_15512_00: the paper's Section 1.1 game rules were checked against hg_win -- players alternate with the cops moving first, pieces move along hyperedges (from u to any v sharing a hyperedge, hg_move; 'not every piece must be moved in every turn' = the stay disjunct), the cops win as soon as one occupies the robber's vertex, and the cop number is the least number of cops with a winning strategy (hg_is_cop_number). The finite-horizon existential is the standard winning condition on a finite position space. O(sqrt(n/k)) is one absolute C quantified outermost and squared to c^2 * k <= C^2 * n, which is the reading the paper itself needs when it observes that the conjecture implies Meyniel's at k = 2. The guard k <= #|T| has teeth (the edgeless one-vertex hypergraph is vacuously k-uniform for every k and would refute the unguarded body) and removes no genuine k-graph. Taking the cop number as a hypothesis does not weaken the statement: at most one c satisfies it and some c always wins (hg_cop_win_card).

axv_2401_00359_01.note: Fox-Sankar-Simkin-Tidor-Zhou Conjecture 6.2: for each k a constant c_k > 0 with ex(n,H) <= O_H(n^{k - c_k/d_max(H)}) for every k-uniform k-partite H. EXPONENT CLEARED TO NAT FORM by raising to the power d_max and multiplying through: (hg_turan F k n)^(hg_dmax F k) * n^ck <= K * n^(k * hg_dmax F k), eventually in n, with c_k depending only on k and the O_H constant K chosen after H. New shared vocabulary: [hg_containsb] (injective, non-induced copy of a pattern), [hg_turan F k n] (max hyperedges of an F-free k-uniform hypergraph on 'I_n), [hg_degeneracy] (least d such that every non-empty vertex set spans a vertex of degree <= d, via ex_minn), [hg_skeleton E i] (the (i+1)-sets inside a hyperedge), [hg_skel_degeneracy] = d_i, [hg_dmax E k] = max over 1 <= i < k. Guards: F != set0 (else d_max = 0 and the cleared inequality degenerates to n^ck <= K, refutable: grounding_X225.v) and 2 <= k (the paper says k >= 3; k = 2 is the Furedi / Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov theorem).

axv_2401_00359_02.note: Fox-Sankar-Simkin-Tidor-Zhou Conjecture 6.4: ex(n,H_L) = n^{3-Theta(1/d)} for the 3-uniform 3-partite hypergraph H_L of a d x d Latin square. Theta(1/d) is rendered with two ABSOLUTE constants a, b > 0 quantified outermost (independent of d and of L) and both inequalities are cleared by raising to the power d without any truncated subtraction: n^(3*d) <= ex^d * n^a (lower) and ex^d * n^b <= n^(3*d) (upper). axv_2208_06858_02.note: Alon-Friedgut-Kalai-Kindler Conjecture 2.6, graph form of Levine's hat problem: lim_t lim_n alpha-bar(K(n)^{box t}) = 0. New local vocabulary in X227.v: [x227_kneser n] (Kneser graph on {set 'I_n}, distinct subsets adjacent iff disjoint - the x != y guard is what makes it irreflexive) and [x227_box_power G t] (t-fold Cartesian power on base's [cartesian_product], with 'K_1 as the empty power). The independence number is coq-graph-theory's [alpha]; the RATIO is kept division-free as q * alpha <= #|V| for eps = 1/q. The iterated limit is rendered 'forall q > 0, exists T, forall t >= T, exists n0, forall n >= n0', i.e. the outer limit over the inner LIMSUP, so no existence claim about the inner limit is smuggled in.

X227:homomorphism-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. axv_2208_06858_02: K(n) is the paper's Kneser graph on the WHOLE cube (all subsets of 'I_n, the empty set included and adjacent to every other vertex), distinct vertices adjacent iff their supports are disjoint -- checked against the paper's own sentence; x227_box_power with 'K_1 as the empty power is the Cartesian (Hamming) power, and G^box 1 = cartesian_product 'K_1 G is a copy of G, so alpha and #|V| are the intended ones. The iterated limit is rendered as 'forall q > 0, exists T, forall t >= T, exists n0, forall n >= n0', i.e. the outer LIMIT over the inner LIMSUP: the outer quantifier is the strong 'exists T, forall t >= T' (not the weaker 'exists t') and nothing asserts that the inner limit exists. bm_003.note: Halin 1970 (Bondy-Murty Appendix A #3), status DISPROVED (Bowler-Erde-Heinig-Lehner-Pitz 2017, Theorem 1.6): hypomorphic infinite graphs embed in each other. Authored faithfully as a refutation target; NO refutation is committed. Carrier is igraph.v's Prop-level [iGraph] with its [infinite_graph] (Dedekind infiniteness). New local vocabulary in X216.v: [x216_embeds] (isomorphism onto a NON-induced subgraph), [x216_del_iso] (G - v isomorphic to H - w, stated on the ambient vertex types so that no eqType is needed) and [x216_hypomorphic]. mathcomp-classical (cardinality.v's countable / #<=) was deliberately NOT used: its predicates go through boolp.asbool, which would make every Print Assumptions report the three classical axioms.

X216:infinite-graph-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. bm_003: 'isomorphic to a subgraph' is the NON-induced containment (injective, adjacency-preserving, nothing said about non-edges), which is the source's reading and the one the Bowler-Erde-Heinig-Lehner-Pitz counterexample refutes, while the hypomorphism clause uses INDUCED vertex-deleted subgraphs: x216_del_iso maps the non-v vertices injectively ONTO the non-w vertices and both preserves and reflects adjacency there, and says nothing about f v. x216_hypomorphic is a bijection phi with G - v isomorphic to H - phi(v) for every v, the standard hypomorphism. Both graphs are required infinite (igraph.v's Dedekind infinite_graph: nat injects into the vertices), and the conclusion is the CONJUNCTION 'each embeds in the other', as the source says. The row is disproved upstream and is authored as a refutation target only: no unconditional refutation is committed anywhere in the package (grounding_X216 proves only that Komega does not embed in the edgeless graph and that the two are not hypomorphic).

axv_2506_08810_03.note: Bonamy-Groenland-Johnston-Morrison-Scott Conjecture 24: for every non-transitive finite tournament T there is a countably infinite T-free tournament every locally finite perturbation of which contains an induced copy of T. The finite tournament is a [diGraph] carrying GTBase.common's [tournament]; the countable side is a [rel nat] (the vertex set IS countably infinite by construction). New local vocabulary in X228.v: [x228_ctournament], [x228_transitive], [x228_induced_copy], [x228_lf_perturbation]. The NONEMPTINESS clause of the perturbation (at least one changed pair) is load-bearing: without it the statement would assert both 'R is T-free' and 'R contains T'.

X228:infinite-graph-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. axv_2506_08810_03: the nonemptiness clause 'exists x != y with R x y != R' x y' is the source's 'perturbing a NONEMPTY locally finite set of pairs', and it is load-bearing -- without it S is a perturbation of itself and the conjecture would assert both 'S is T-free' and 'S contains T'. 'Locally finite' as 'for each v there is N with R' v u = R v u for all u >= N' is exactly finiteness of the changed set at each vertex on nat, and quantifying it per-vertex (not globally) is right; since both R and R' are tournaments, constraining only the arcs out of v also constrains those into v. x228_induced_copy (injective f with (x -- y) = R (f x) (f y) for distinct x, y) is induced containment, which for tournaments coincides with containment. A relation on nat IS a countably infinite vertex set, so no cardinality layer is needed, and x228_ctournament (irreflexive, exactly one arc between distinct vertices) is the tournament axiom. The non-transitivity guard negates transitivity of the arc relation and is necessary, as the source explains.

bm_062.note: Kotzig's unique k-path conjecture: for k >= 3 no graph has a unique path of length k between every two DISTINCT vertices. The Rocq body is the negation of the unique-path property, universally quantified over k >= 3 and over G, guarded by 1 < #|G| (on a graph with fewer than two vertices the property holds vacuously, which would make the statement false for trivial reasons). Paths of length k are lists p with path (--) x p, size p = k, uniq (x :: p) and last x p = y; uniqueness is exists!. The distinct-pairs reading is the one under which k = 2 is the Friendship Theorem, as the corpus context states.

bm_065.note: Bondy: some positive constant c makes every 3-connected cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph contain a cycle of length at least c*n. The positive real constant is encoded as the positive rational p/q by two positive naturals, the conclusion being the cross-multiplied p * #|G| <= q * size c; this is equivalent to the real form because every positive real constant can be lowered to a positive rational one. Cyclic edge connectivity is local vocabulary (x212_edge_cut, x212_cycle_within): every vertex set whose two sides both contain a cycle has an edge cut of at least 4 edges. Cubic is regular G 3 on a simple graph.

bm_066.note: Birmele-Bondy-Reed: if any two cycles on at least k vertices meet, then some set of AT MOST k vertices meets every cycle on at least k vertices. The guard 3 <= k is load-bearing: for k <= 2 the hypothesis only says that any two cycles meet, which holds in K_5, while no single vertex or pair meets all cycles of K_5, so the unguarded statement is false; the conjecture is posed for k >= 3. 'A set of k vertices' is read as at most k (a set of exactly k vertices need not exist when #|G| < k).

axv_2304_03567_04.note: Bessy-Thomasse-Viennot Conjecture 1. The forward cover is defined in the paper (body/request.tex of the arXiv e-print): a set of vertex orderings in which every pair {x, y} has x, y or y, x as a forward pair, i.e. joined by a directed path whose vertices increase in the ordering. An ordering is an injective ranking into nat (x231_forward_arc: the arcs that go up), the cover a sequence of rankings (x231_forward_cover), and the pairs are pairs of distinct vertices (x231_forward_pair: a forward path from the earlier endpoint to the later one). O(log n) is read as constants c and n0 with a cover of size at most c * trunc_log 2 n for every strong digraph on n >= n0 vertices. The row is refuted in applications/forward_cover_disproof.v (logarithmic_forward_cover_disproved): the diamond chain on 3m vertices needs m orderings.

x231_forward_arc.reason: The forward arcs of a vertex ranking (arcs that go up), the building block of forward paths in arXiv:2304.03567; no shared vertex-ordering path primitive exists in digraph-theory.

x231_forward_pair.reason: A pair forward connected in an ordering (a forward path from the earlier endpoint to the later one), the paper's forward pair.

x231_forward_cover.reason: The paper's forward cover: vertex orderings (injective rankings) in which every pair of distinct vertices is forward connected in one member.

X231.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-10-26 (verifier Arthur): 1/1 PASS. arxiv:2304.03567#04 (Bessy-Thomasse-Viennot Conjecture 1): the paper's forward cover (body/request.tex) is a set of vertex orderings in which every pair {x, y} has x, y or y, x forward, a forward pair being joined by a directed path of forward arcs, the arcs xy with x before y (introduction.tex, definitions.tex). An ordering is exactly an injective ranking into nat (u before v iff r u < r v); x231_forward_arc is the paper's forward arc (a loop is never forward); connect of the forward arcs is a forward path, since a forward walk strictly raises r and so repeats no vertex; x231_forward_pair is the paper's 'x, y or y, x'; the pairs are V choose 2 (x != y). A sequence of rankings and a set of orderings bound each other (list the set; a sequence induces at most size-many orderings). O(log n) as exists c n0 with size <= c * trunc_log 2 n for n >= n0 is the usual reading: for n >= 2, log2 n <= 2 floor(log2 n), a natural c loses nothing, and n0 exempts small n as O(.) does. strongb is strong connectivity ([forall x, forall y, connect arc x y]). The statement is neither weaker nor stronger than the source, so the refutation in applications/forward_cover_disproof.v (the diamond chain on 3m vertices, a loopless strong digraph whose m twin pairs need m orderings) refutes the conjecture as the paper states it.

erdos_625.note: Erdos Problems #625, Erdos and Gimbel (ErGi93; pinned status open, $1000): for G(n,1/2), for every M, with probability -> 1, zeta(G) + M <= chi(G) (x261_cochromatic_exact; classes induce complete or empty graphs). Convergence in probability, as Heckel (2408.13839v2 l.231; 2409.17614v2 l.251, l.257) and Steiner (2408.02400v2 l.113-115) read it. Open at the pin; He24, St24b and He24c are partial; Petkov's linked claim (625-claim.pdf, 10 September 2026) is cited, not verified.

erdos_717.note: Erdos Problems #717, Erdos and Fajtlowicz (ErFa81; pinned status solved): sigma(G), the largest k such that G contains a subdivision of K_k (x261_clique_subdivision_order); (chi(G) trunc_log 2 n)^2 <= C n sigma(G)^2 for every graph on n vertices. Proved before the pin: Fox, Lee and Sudakov, arXiv:1107.1920v3, Theorem 1.1 (source.tex l.130-132), subdivisions as in l.92-95.

erdos_760.note: Erdos Problems #760, Erdos and Gimbel (ErGi93; pinned status solved): if chi(G) = m >= 2 (load-bearing: log 1 = 0), a subgraph H, not necessarily induced (has_subgraph), has m <= C k trunc_log 2 m for every cochromatic colouring of H with k colours. Proved before the pin: Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov, Theorem 1.1 (AKS97.txt l.29-30); the linked Lean proof (plby f2462b28, C = 32) is an external proof.

erdos_797.note: Erdos Problems #797, Erdos (AlBe76; pinned status solved): f(d) = o(d^2), f the largest acyclic chromatic number of a graph of maximum degree exactly d (x261_acyclic_colourable: proper, every cycle sees three colours); for every q >= 1, eventually q k <= d^2. "Estimate f(d)" is not formalised. Proved before the pin: Alon, McDiarmid and Reed (1991), Theorem 1.1 (p.278) and Proposition 2.2.

erdos_799.note: Erdos Problems #799, Erdos, Rubin and Taylor (ERT80; pinned status solved): almost all graphs (G(n,1/2), fg_whp) have chi_L(G) <= n %/ q for every q >= 1 (x261_choosable_b, equivalent to GTBase choosable, grounding_X261). Proved before the pin: Alon (1992), Corollary 1.3 (Al92.txt l.66-67): ch(G(n,1/2)) <= c n log log n / log n with probability -> 1.

x261_cochromatic_at_most.reason: The cochromatic colouring of erdos:625 and erdos:760 (pinned texts: each colour class induces a complete or an empty graph), as a Boolean over upstream cliqueb and stable so that it can describe a G(n,1/2) event; Chromatic.conjectures.XE2's xe2_cochromatic_colouring is the same notion as a Prop (grounding_X261's g261_cochromatic_at_mostP reflects it).

x261_cochromatic_exact.reason: zeta(G) of erdos:625 (the pinned text's cochromatic number, the minimum number of colours), relational and Boolean.

x261_topological_clique.reason: G contains a subdivision of K_k, erdos:717 (pinned text; Fox, Lee and Sudakov, arXiv:1107.1920v3, source.tex l.92-95: the edges replaced by internally vertex-disjoint paths). chromatic-theory has no non-induced notion of it: GTBase's induced_subdivision is induced and base.v's subdivision is uniform.

x261_clique_subdivision_order.reason: sigma(G) of erdos:717 (pinned text: the maximal k such that G contains a subdivision of K_k), relational.

x261_acyclic_colourable.reason: The acyclic colouring of erdos:797 (pinned text: proper, no cycle containing only two colours; Alon, McDiarmid and Reed p.277) into 'I_k; Chromatic.conjectures.U4's acyclic_colouring is its list form, equivalent with whole-palette lists (g261_acyclic_colourableE).

x261_choosable_b.reason: The list colouring of erdos:799 (pinned text: lists of k colours) as a Boolean over the palette 'I_(#|G| * k), so that it can describe a G(n,1/2) event; grounding_X261 proves it equivalent to GTBase's choosable over any finite palette (g261_choosable_bE).

x260_clique_size_count.reason: The number of different sizes of cliques of a graph, cliques being maximal complete subgraphs (erdos:927 pinned text; Erdos, On cliques in graphs, Israel J. Math. 4 (1966), p.233), over GTBase maximal_clique.

x260_clique_size_number.reason: g(n) of erdos:927: the maximum number of different sizes of cliques that can occur in a graph on n vertices (pinned text; Er66b p.233).

x260_log_star.reason: log_*(n) of erdos:927, "the number of iterated logarithms such that log ... log n < 1" (pinned text), with base 2 and integer floors (equal to the real count for n >= 1).

x260_copy.reason: A copy of H on [n] in Alon, Graph-codes, arXiv:2301.13305v2 (source.tex l.89-91), exact as in Versteegen, arXiv:2310.19891v2 (linear_graph_codes.tex l.98): an edge set equal to the image of E(H) under an injective vertex map.

x260_code.reason: An H-code (Alon, arXiv:2301.13305v2, source.tex l.86-91): a family of graphs on [n] containing no two members whose symmetric difference is a copy of H.

std_guo_kang_zwaneveld_conjecture.note: Guo, Kang and Zwaneveld, Conjecture 2 of arXiv:2411.06941v1 (pinned status open): for every G, d and k, chi(G) <= k iff G boxtimes K_(d+1) (x264_strong_product) has a d-defective colouring by 'I_k (x264_defective_colourable), i.e. chi(G) = chi^d(G boxtimes K_(d+1)); direction -> always holds (g264_lift). FALSE at the pin: Norin and Steiner, arXiv:2504.01548v1, Theorem 1.2 (main.tex l.124-126), for every d >= 2 a G with chi^d(G boxtimes K_(d+1)) <= 2d^3 + 2d^2 + d + 3 < chi(G).

axv_1803_10962_01.note: Dvorak, Esperet, Kang and Ozeki, arXiv:1803.10962v2 (dp1.tex l.168; pinned status solved): a natural C such that every positive k with C^2 d (trunc_log 2 n)^2 <= k^2 single-conflict colours every d-degenerate simple graph on n vertices (X210's x210_conflict_k_colourable_under_rat_bound G k 1 k, the exactly-one form by g264_single_conflictE); the guard 0 < k is load-bearing (g264_sc_guard_teeth). True at the pin: Bradshaw and Masarik, arXiv:2112.06333v2, Theorem 1.7 (SCCmain.tex l.241-246).

axv_2405_14795_01.note: Alon, Defant and Kravitz, Question 3.3 (arXiv:2405.14795v1, main.tex l.410-412; pinned status open), as its affirmative answer: for odd n, every two proper edge-colourings of K_n into one palette 'I_r (GTBase proper_edge_colouring) admit vertex permutations s1, s2 with chi1(s1^-1 e) <> chi2(s2^-1 e) at every edge e (x264_rainbow_stacking, l.106). Open at the pin; yes for n = 3 and 5 (l.414), no for n = 2^k - 2 (Proposition 3.2).

x264_strong_rel.reason: The adjacency of the strong product G boxtimes H of studies:std_guo_kang_zwaneveld_conjecture (Guo, Kang and Zwaneveld, arXiv:2411.06941v1, improper-arXiv.tex l.125: distinct, and in each coordinate equal or adjacent), the union of GTBase's box_rel and tensor_rel (grounding_X264's g264_strong_relE).

x264_strong_product.reason: The strong product G boxtimes H as an sgraph over x264_strong_rel. Neither coq-graph-theory nor GTBase has one (base.v has the cartesian and tensor products), and extremal X191's x191_clique_blowup is a blow-up of K_m only, in another package. With H = K_t it is Norin and Steiner's form (arXiv:2504.01548v1 l.114; g264_strong_KE).

x264_defective_colourable.reason: A d-defective (d-improper) colouring by 'I_k (2411.06941v1 l.178; 2504.01548v1 l.110): every vertex has at most d neighbours of its own colour, chi^d being the least such k. Chromatic X218's x218_defective_chromatic_class_le is a class-level notion with the defect bound chosen first; defect 0 is a proper colouring (g264_defective0).

x264_rainbow_stacking.reason: A rainbow stacking of two edge-colourings of K_n into a common palette 'I_r (Alon, Defant and Kravitz, arXiv:2405.14795v1, main.tex l.106, with m = 2): vertex permutations s1, s2 with chi1(s1^-1 e) <> chi2(s2^-1 e) at every edge e.

erdos_777.note: Erdos Problems #777, Daykin and Erdos (Gu83; pinned status solved, resolved in some other way than a proof or disproof): the three asked clauses on the comparability graph G_F of a family F of subsets of [n] (x263_comparable_pairs), as a conjunction. FALSE at the pin: Alon and Frankl (Graphs Combin. 1 (1985), Example 6.1) refute the second; the first (Alon, Das, Glebov, Sudakov, arXiv:1411.4196v1) and the third (Alon-Frankl, Section 2) hold.

erdos_1031.note: Erdos Problems #1031, Erdos, Fajtlowicz and Staton (Er93 p.340; pinned PROVED): a graph on n vertices with no clique and no stable set on at least 10 log_2 n vertices (n^10 <= 2^k, base 2 exactly) has an induced d-regular subgraph G[S] with 0 < d and d + 1 < |S| and log_2 n <= q |S|, for n >= N. Proved by Promel and Rodl (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 88 (1999)): induced universality for every constant c > 0 (publisher abstract).

erdos_1077.note: Erdos Problems #1077, Erdos and Simonovits (ErSi70 pp.388-389; pinned status solved, answered negatively; page label DISPROVED): for every rational eps = r/p and alpha = a/b in (0, 1) there are D and N such that every G on n >= N vertices with at least n^(1+alpha) edges has a D-balanced subgraph (Delta <= D delta) on m > n^(1-alpha) vertices with at least eps m^(1+alpha) edges; eps universal as in the original. FALSE at the pin: K_(s,n-s) with s about 3 n^alpha refutes it for every 0 < alpha < 1/2 (the page's discussion).

axv_2004_10180_00.note: Conlon, Fox, Sudakov and Zhao, arXiv:2004.10180v3, after Corollary 1.4 (pinned open), as its affirmative answer: the exponent 3/2 is best possible, i.e. for every q >= 1, C and N some C_5-free G (no C_5 subgraph) on n >= N vertices needs more than C^(1/(2q)) n^(3/2 - 1/q) deleted edges to become triangle-free. v3 leaves it open (PDF pp.3 and 17).
